name: Khedive Ismail

summary.text: Ismāʿīl Pasha was Khedive of Egypt from 1863 to 1879. Britannica states that Egypt's national debt stood at £7 million when he took power and had risen to almost £100 million by 1876. In November 1875, facing default, he sold Egypt's shares in the Suez Canal Company to the British government for £4 million, financed by N M Rothschild & Sons. In 1876 he defaulted and, by decree of 2 May 1876, the Caisse de la Dette Publique was created with commissioners named by France, Britain, Austria and Italy to service the debt; Evelyn Baring served as a commissioner from 1877 to 1879. Ismail was deposed in 1879.

facts.claim: Britannica states that the Egyptian national debt stood at £7,000,000 when Ismail took power in 1863 and had risen to almost £100,000,000 by 1876.
facts.quote: the Egyptian national debt stood at £7,000,000 when Ismāʿīl took power, and by 1876 it had risen to almost £100,000,000.

facts.claim: In an 1884 Commons debate, Egypt's nine loans of 1862–1879 were put at a nominal £77 million with net proceeds of about £55.6 million; the contractors of the 1862–1873 loans were criticised for indulging Ismail's extravagance.
facts.quote: the loans from 1862 to 1873 drew heavy criticism for the contractors who indulged Ismail Pasha's extravagance.

facts.claim: In November 1875, owing to Ismail's bankruptcy, Disraeli's government bought nearly half the shares in the Suez Canal Company; because Parliament was not sitting, the £4,000,000 was borrowed from the Rothschilds.
facts.quote: Since Parliament was not in session at the time, Disraeli borrowed £4,000,000 from the Rothschilds

sources.title: Lionel de Rothschild and the Suez Canal

facts.claim: On 21 February 1876 the House of Commons took a supply vote of £4,080,000 for the Suez Canal shares.

sources.title: Supply—£4,080,000 Suez Canal Shares, House of Commons

facts.claim: The Caisse de la Dette Publique was created in 1876 to service Egypt's debt, with members named by France, Britain, Austria and Italy.
facts.quote: The Caisse de la Dette Publique was created in 1876 to service Egypt's debt, and its members were named by France, Britain, Austria, and Italy.

facts.claim: The House of Commons debated Egyptian finance and Mr Cave's mission on 5 August 1876, following Ismail's default.

connections.claim: Evelyn Baring went to Egypt in 1877 as representative of the British holders of Egyptian bonds on the Egyptian Public Debt Commission (Caisse de la Dette), serving as commissioner 1877–1879; he was the prime mover behind a Commission of Inquiry into Egyptian finances, resigned when Ismail rejected his advice, and returned as British controller of the debt after Ismail was deposed in 1879.
connections.quote: he served as representative of the British holders of Egyptian bonds on the recently created Egyptian Public Debt Commission.

sources.title: Baring, Evelyn, (1841-1917), 1st Earl of Cromer, statesman

connections.claim: Lionel de Rothschild alerted Disraeli to the chance of buying the Khedive's Suez Canal shares and N M Rothschild & Sons lent the British government the £4 million for the 1875 purchase.
connections.quote: Lionel Rothschild alerted Disraeli to the chance of buying up shares in the Suez Canal Company.

sources.title: Lionel de Rothschild and the Suez Canal

openQuestions: The site's '£68 million nominal, £46 million received, 1862–1873' was not found; Hansard 1884 gives £77 million nominal and about £55.6 million net for nine loans 1862–1879. Check Landes, 'Bankers and Pashas' (1958).
The site says Britain joined the Caisse in 1877; Britannica lists Britain among the four naming powers from 1876, while Baring's own appointment dates from 1877.
The site names Hermann Oppenheim as arranger of several loans; no source consulted addressed this.
The 1880 Law of Liquidation, the corvée and the muqabala were not covered by the sources consulted.
The exact share count (176,602, about 44%) appeared only in an AI-generated encyclopedia and is not relied on.
